This cluster gathers the accounts of the ultimate that are not classically theistic but make the same bid against structure: Spinozist pantheism (§5.3.1), Neoplatonism (§5.3.2), process theology (§5.3.3), and Madhyamaka emptiness (§5.3.4). Each names or reconceives ultimacy — one infinite substance, the One beyond being, creative process, or emptiness. Some place the ultimate prior to familiar structure; others identify ultimacy with an immanent or dependent order rather than trying to transcend it.

The single question carries over: can the account reach its ultimate without leaning on the structure it was meant to stand free of? The finding is relocation rather than refutation. The candidates divide: articulated priority claims incur determinate-role burdens; immanent and process accounts may be compatible with the structural floor while revising ultimacy; strict apophatic and anti-thesis positions leave an open semantic or dialectical seam.
